newsitem.title: UK: Record fine for Deutsche UK fund arm.
newsitem.headline: Record fine for Deutsche UK fund arm.

text.p: Investment watchdog IMRO on Wednesday slapped a record two million pound ($3.3 million) fine on the British fund managment arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank for a catalogue of rule breaches and management failings.

The Investment Management Regulatory Organisation imposed costs of a million pounds on two units of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management and said they had not informed it about management problems, adding that at least one MGAM board member knew of the problems by April 1996. Problems at three MGAM funds did not emerge until September of last year.
Record fine for Deutsche UK fund arm =2

IMRO said it had yet to reach its conclusions about the individuals responsible for the management and supervision of the Morgan Grenfell European Growth Trust, the Morgan Grenfell Europa Fund and the Dublin-based Morgan Grenfell European Capital Growth Fund.

IMRO chief executive Phillip Thorpe said the mismanagement of the three funds had "caused unnecessary concern to an enormous number of investors". The funds were temporarily suspended last September when serious irregularities in valuations of unlisted securities were discovered.

Around 90,000 retail investors had money invested in funds, two of which were managed by former MGAM fund manager Peter Young whose activities are under investigation by Britain's Serious Fraud Office. Young has denied any criminal activity.

IMRO said the irregularities were connected with, but not limited to, the activities of Peter Young, who carried out the day-to-day management of European Growth and Capital Growth. It said one of the MGAM units had failed to ensure that fund managers were adequately supervised despite concerns about various aspects of their business.
